### CHAPTER VII. ###

That the Lord our good God, notwithstanding all our former transgressions and our stubbornness in the same, still nevertheless offers grace and peace, if only we will turn from them with our whole hearts to God. And what the test may be, whether one truly wishes to repent or not.

<margin>The Lord God still offers peace to those who have behaved badly, provided they now sincerely better themselves.</margin>
But now, behold the great and unspeakable benevolence and long-suffering of God. Whereas He is so justly prepared for war against us, and could—with a single turn of His hand—overturn the highest to the lowest, confound all our counsel, weaken the hearts of our field commanders and young soldiers, and make us a prey to our enemy (just as we have well deserved): yet He is still long-suffering toward us. He allows us to be warned first before He chooses to strike; He allows His peace to be offered to us now, and has it proclaimed so that if we will now still turn from our evil ways to Him (even now, when He can and may so readily destroy us), if we will now still put away our abominations from before His eyes, then He will still receive us in grace, have mercy upon us, and build us up, and not overthrow us. For thus much our text says: if we will not repent <note>Original Dutch: "bekeeren," which implies a turning back or conversion.</note>, then the Lord will "turn us over" <note>The author uses a wordplay between "bekeeren" (repentance/turning to God) and "om-keeren" (overturning/destruction).</note>; and that is explained elsewhere thus: that if we will indeed repent, and ensure that others repent, then our wicked unrighteousness shall not be our ruin and downfall. For thus speaks the Lord: *I have no pleasure in the death of one who dies, therefore turn and live.* Ezekiel 18:32.

<column-break/>

<margin>Therefore, if we will now still better ourselves, then God will stand on our side, and help us against all our enemies.</margin>
Take heed then, you Christian people; see how you are now minded toward your sins. You see here the Lord God Almighty in a posture of war, and you still have your choice whether you want the Lord of Hosts to set Himself for you or against you. If you will repent, then the Lord your God will turn to your side and strike all your enemies in their rear parts. If, on the other hand, you refuse to repent, then the Lord will strengthen the arm of your enemy and will overturn you yourself. Ezekiel 30:24. If you then wish to keep your sins with you any longer and excuse them, then the Lord God will keep Himself by your enemy and destroy you. If you will not listen to the word of the Lord to leave your sins, then the Lord God will leave you. Indeed, if you do not better all the abuses that have been so often pointed out to you from the word of the Lord, then the Lord God will, in His own time, ruin your state and lay waste to your land. If, conversely, you will go against your sins, then the Lord God will go with you against your enemy and deliver you out of all your troubles.

Consider then, I say once more, how you are minded in this matter: will you repent or not? Behold, you are all alike before the face of the Lord; pour out your heart now, examine yourself, see how you are minded, and answer now to the question of the Lord: *If you will return, O Israel, return to me.*

We hope that you all say alike in your hearts before God (who knows the hearts and the kidneys <note>A common biblical idiom referring to one's innermost thoughts and emotions.</note>) that you indeed wish to turn to the Lord your God, that you no longer wish to chase after your sins, but to cling to the Lord your God.

# ZION’S TRUMPET #

<margin>But no one can be said to truly want to improve who does not strive for their improvement with seriousness and sincerity.</margin>
Are you then so minded? Is this truly your unfeigned intention? Then consider here what it means to truly desire to turn to the Lord your God: it is not—as we heard above—to wish so faintly and weakly that one might be released from one's sins and be able to serve God pleasingly; for almost all people wish to be converted. But to **will** to repent <note>Original Dutch: *bekeeren*, meaning to turn back or convert.</note> means here to desire to strive for one’s conversion with such seriousness as the weight of the matter and the high majesty of our God justly requires and demands.

<margin>A point which very many do not notice, and they quickly convince themselves that they indeed wish to repent, when it is nonetheless not the case.</margin>
This must be carefully noted in every respect, for great deception hides within man, and the spiritual enemy working beneath it leads many to be deceived in this. When the poor, ignorant person hears and learns that before God—even though he has behaved quite poorly against his God, and even though the Lord his God is already prepared and equipped for punishment against him—he can still escape all hardship and find grace with God if he only wishes to turn from his evil ways to God in time, then the ignorant person immediately blesses himself in his state. He quickly allows himself to believe that all is well with him, for he thinks to himself: "Praise be to God, I am not of such an evil heart or mind that I would not want to repent, or that I would want to willfully continue in my sins and transgressions. No, the Lord knows it, my sins grieve me from the heart, and I have no intention to continue in them, but

<column-break/>

I wish to turn from them from the heart; so God will also be merciful to me, and then it shall go well with me."

Thus many an ignorant person thinks, and thus he speaks to himself accordingly in his actions; whereas, if he were examined according to the word of the Lord and the truth of the Most High, he does not truly have such a will as he ought to have to repent, but has only a faint, weak desire of a leopard <note>This likely alludes to Jeremiah 13:23: "Can the Ethiopian change his skin or the leopard its spots?" The author uses it to describe a superficial desire that never results in actual change.</note> for repentance. Yet the matter stands thus: with the pursuit of repentance from our sins to God, we must desire and *will* it with the greatest seriousness and diligence that we can or may, should we prove that indeed our hearts are sincere in this before the Lord our God.

<margin>As is irrefutably shown by the fact that they leave many things unimproved which they could easily better if they only willed it.</margin>
But that many people truly do not have the will to turn from their evil sins to God, while they nonetheless boast greatly of it, is irrefutably shown by the fact that these same people leave very many things unimproved in themselves, which they could easily enough improve if they only seriously wished to improve them. Thus you find many there who are very fond of drinking <note>Original Dutch: *dzanck*, an archaic spelling of *drank* (drink/drunkenness).</note>, and when spoken to about it, they testify with great seriousness that they wish to guard against it from now on; and yet, when there is no other occasion to restrain them than the reverence they owe to God and the obedience they must show to His commandments, they fall every time (as often as any external occasion is given to them) again and again into the same sin; and these nonetheless still convince themselves that they truly...

They only deceive themselves, and others who believe them, when they boast so loudly that they indeed wish to turn to God. Is it then not a hardened hypocrisy <note>Original: *gebeystheydt*, meaning insincerity or a feigned show of piety.</note> when the poor person persists in constantly letting it be heard that he indeed wants to convert to God, yet he himself does not improve those things out of respect and reverence for God—which he knows well enough how to improve out of respect for some worldly matter, whenever an opportunity arises? Yes, mark what we say: suppose there stood a Spaniard <note>A "sworn enemy" in the context of the Dutch Revolt; representing a clear and present mortal danger.</note>, one of our sworn enemies, with a naked sword and a loaded pistol against our breast, and should threaten to shoot us dead if we did not guard ourselves against some of the outward quirks <note>Original: *nucken*, meaning bad habits, whims, or moral flaws.</note> that we previously pointed out, which circulate so commonly among us; and if we, on the other hand, would not perform those outward duties that we previously pointed out as being so greatly neglected among us—then we would surely, sincerely want to abstain from them to preserve our life; then we would surely also be able to do it or leave it. I speak of such things as are done with the cooperation of our body. Well, see here the great unbelief or the great hypocrisy of men. God the Lord is introduced to us here in our text with a naked sword in one hand, with a deadly firearm in

<column-break/>

the other hand, wherewith He wishes to wound men, not only unto death, but unto eternal damnation, if they will not leave their aforementioned quirks and practice the required duties. If people believed this, and if they then also sincerely, accordingly, wanted to convert because of it from their evil ways, would they then not truly be able to improve a thousand things that now still lie there unimproved? Would they not indeed be able to leave many vile habits that they still do? Would they not quickly be able to do and carry out many holy duties, to which they now do not even lift a finger? Everyone can easily perceive that it is so. When, however, this does not happen, and when people nevertheless remain so loud-mouthed in boasting that they indeed want to convert, and so gently set themselves at rest and peace regarding it, then it is surely evident everywhere by this the great unbelief or hypocrisy of those same men; therefore these must also rightly let themselves be warned to take better heed, if they do not wish to be set as a target <note>Original: *doele*, an archery target; suggesting God will aim His judgment at them.</note> by God, as a people that truly does not want to convert, as a people that does not hear the Lord their God, nor wants to improve, Jeremiah 7:27 <note>The verse says: "So you shall speak all these words to them, but they will not listen to you. You shall call to them, but they will not answer you."</note>.

Which we here gladly say and repeat, and say once more very clearly: for indeed many people deceive themselves miserably and almost willfully in this, and provoke the Lord their God to the highest anger, He who sees well enough that they regard Him, nor His commandments, by far not as much as they do a portion of paltry trifles of this world, which perish with use.

### CHAPTER VIII.

That people commonly begin to seek excuses and make objections when they are earnestly urged toward any duty; and what the primary objections are through which many today are held back from pursuing the reformation of abuses as the current state of the Reformed Christian world <note>The "Reformed Christian world" refers to the international community of Protestant churches following the tradition of John Calvin, particularly prominent in the Dutch Republic where this was written.</note> requires.

<margin>
This laxity <note>Original: *slappieheydt*, referring to a lack of spiritual vigor or commitment.</note> cannot be excused by any kind of sugar-coating, even though people are very prone to seeking excuses when they are earnestly exhorted to some Christian duty.
</margin>

But now I greatly fear that many, hearing that the practice of conversion <term>conversion</term> <note>From the Dutch *bekeeringe*, meaning a total turning of the heart toward God and a change in behavior.</note> and the improvement of those things which we must take in hand must be done so earnestly and so boldly if we are to obtain the offered peace of God—and so that the Lord our God does not attack us as if He were our enemy—will begin to seek excuses there. They will try to convince themselves that although God considers [these things], they need not be taken so strictly or so sharply; they think it will go well enough for us if we just make things reasonably right, even if we do not take God’s cause as precisely as some insist. This, I say, we fear; and therefore we shall, for the sake of completeness, proceed to handle these matters. First, we shall remove some objections through which we have noticed many are held back from the earnest practice of true conversion, as the present condition of the Christian world requires. Second-

<column-break/>

ly, in addition to everything that has been said, we shall present some motives for why we should practice the aforementioned required conversion. And thirdly, we shall point out some means by which the necessary conversion might be promoted and brought about. And all of that we shall, finally, apply to our own souls.

<margin>
And also they readily find many excuses or objections to pull their necks out from under the Lord’s yoke <note>A biblical metaphor for submission to God's authority.</note>.
</margin>

The objections and excuses that many people usually put forward when they are earnestly exhorted to a sincere practice of conversion are very numerous. Since we have spoken of these at length in our *Treatise on Conversion* regarding the occasion of the proper observance of a Day of Fasting and Prayer <note>Original: *Vasten-biddaechs*. These were official days of national repentance called by the Dutch government during times of crisis like war or plague.</note>, we do not intend to speak of them again here. Instead, we shall only touch upon some specific objections or excuses mostly relevant to the present discussion, and those which we have noticed (above others) that hold back many people today from applying themselves with such diligence to the improvement of things, as the current state and condition of the Reformed Christian world otherwise rightly indicates and requires. And according to our findings, these are primarily the following:

First, that we are not so strictly bound to everything taught to us in the word of the Lord, that we would surely fail if we did not practice it all.

Second, that many things are also taught by the Ministers <note>Original: *Predicanten*, the clergy of the Reformed Church.</note> which do not appear so clearly from the...

### CHAPTER IX.

#### Answering the first objection: that
#### we are not bound to practice
#### exactly everything taught to us

<margin>But it is the bounden duty of the Christian people in this case to search the Holy Scripture all the more diligently to learn whether that which the Ministers require in the matter of morals is truly well-founded in God’s word, even if at first it does not seem to be there.</margin>

Therefore, if the Scripture were to provide us a report on all these—as it truly does according to *2 Timothy 3:16-17* <note>original: "2 Tim. 3.16.17." This passage states that all Scripture is God-breathed and useful for teaching, rebuking, correcting and training in righteousness.</note>—one should not always expect an express command, but must necessarily be satisfied with a sound judgment and the logical consequence of matters to determine one's bounden duty.

->Thus it is worth the effort in every way<-

whenever something is preached and taught to us by the *Ministers* <note>The term "Predicanten" refers specifically to the ordained clergy in the Dutch Reformed tradition.</note> regarding what to do or what to leave undone, that we diligently look into and search the Holy Scriptures concerning it, like those of *Berea* <note>The Bereans are praised in Acts 17:11 for examining the Scriptures daily to see if what the Apostle Paul taught was true.</note>, to see whether the Scriptures also speak thus or imply such things, or not. And truly, whoever will not take the trouble to do so, but merely satisfies himself in general by convincing his conscience that what the *Minister* teaches is not clearly stated in the Holy Scripture, and that he is therefore not bound to it—that person stands in his own light and betrays his own soul. Especially if he is conscious that he himself does not usually read or search the Holy Scripture diligently, so that he does not have much grounded knowledge of everything that might be spread throughout the Holy Scripture. Such a person, if he does not wish to willfully gamble with his soul, has every fair reason to consider his own affairs suspicious: namely, when he ventures to arrange his affairs quite differently than his regular Teacher (who must care for his soul and practices daily in the Scripture to bring forth old and new things for his edification) is teaching him. For pray, what

<column-break/>

sense is there in this: that while everyone else is believed in their own craft (when they are seen as merely pious and decent people), the men of God alone should not be believed, even when one can bring no scriptural proof against their requirement? Thus it is entirely fair (we say) that all those who are accustomed to speak lightly, dismissing many things the *Ministers* teach (as if they were not bound by them, because they do not see them expressly laid down in the word of the Lord), should at least take the trouble to also daily search the Holy Scripture diligently and weigh everything well according to the Scripture, whether the *Ministers’* claim holds firm or not. For it is surely not at all becoming that we should mock the blind *Papists* <note>A historical term for Roman Catholics, used here to criticize those who follow religious leaders without personal study of the Bible.</note>, who rely on the sayings of their *Pastors* and want only to believe what they believe, even though they do not know what they believe, and even though that has never been proven to them from the word of the Lord; and that we, on the other hand, would neither want to believe what the *Ministers* tell us, nor take the trouble to properly investigate in the word of the Lord whether what they preach to us is truly required of us in God’s word or not. This would surely be very absurd and in no way becoming of the *Reformed Christian* people, who have made a profession that they wish to conduct all their affairs according to the word of the Lord. Therefore, in this case, God's word must be diligently searched by everyone. For this, these reasons from each of us must also be thoroughly considered.

Do we not, in temporal things—in cases a thousand times more trivial—exercise just as much foresight, diligence, and ingenuity?

### CHAPTER XI.

->Answering the third objection, taken from the claim that we are not idolaters, but still have pure worship among us, even if we are somewhat lax in other things.<-

<margin>III. Objection. We are not idolaters; we have pure worship among us.</margin>

The third objection is this: That we are not idolaters, but still have the clean, pure worship of God among us; and therefore, even if things go somewhat poorly with us in other matters, we are nonetheless in no danger. For it is not seen that God drove away his people Israel as long as they 

<column-break/>

maintained pure worship. See, with this many people also flatter themselves, as we have observed, and they set themselves at ease, promising themselves many good days ahead, even though they have very great reason for fear.

<margin>Look at us, and therefore even if things go somewhat poorly in other matters, we are nonetheless in no danger. Answer: How we enjoy the teaching, yet still lead an impure life, and how we have heavier punishment to expect.</margin>

Answer: It is a wonder that we can make such conclusions: namely, that where God the Lord, out of great and unspeakable grace, has been pleased to place us like a vineyard in a fertile spot, and to hedge us in in the best possible way by prescribing a good order, and to plant us with the noblest vines—which are the potencies of pure, clean, and sound doctrine—that we are nonetheless in no danger, even if, in place of bringing forth grapes, we bring forth only wild grapes and lead an unchristian life. Indeed, that we are so dull and foolish, and allow ourselves to be so grossly misled by the Deceiver, that we can imagine that precisely because God the Lord has taken much trouble with us and spent much on us—so that we might indeed be fruitful in all good works—we shall still be spared even if we remain unfruitful. Thus, we lay as a foundation for our comfort and excuse the very thing that God the Lord, and all fair reason, lays as a foundation for our terror and approaching difficulties. He testifies of His vineyard that precisely because He had planted His vineyard with noble vines—that is, with the very best doctrine—and yet it still brought forth stinking grapes <note>The author refers to Isaiah 5, where God judges a vineyard that produces "wild" or "stinking" grapes despite receiving perfect care.</note>, He would take away His hedge, so that it might...

It also appears that these people—who comfort themselves with the thought that even if their lives are but poor, they will nonetheless be spared because they are no **idolaters** and have the pure worship of God among them—assume that pure, clean worship <note>original: "Godts-dienst" — this term refers to the external practice of religion or "service to God."</note> consists only in the brain, and that the heart has nothing to do with it; and that the holy [truth] should only serve to fill the brain with knowledge and science of Divine doctrine, and not also to fill the heart with desires and contemplations of a godly life. But the holy truth of God judges quite differently: indeed, the Apostle **James** testifies to us very explicitly that the pure and undefiled worship before God and the Father is this: To visit orphans and widows in their affliction [and] to keep oneself unspotted from the world. **James 1:27.** Which these people do not practice, though they nonetheless rely on such pure and clean worship.

But this is always certain: to join to the purity of doctrine a pure and godly life.

...which we shall set out at length here) runs as follows:

We see that the beautiful, glorious Churches of **Brabant**, **Flanders**, **Hainaut**, and elsewhere are perishing, and are being brought by force under the yoke of idolatry <note>A common Protestant term for Roman Catholic practices, particularly the veneration of images and the Mass</note>, and the remnant scattered across the four corners of the world, much as it happened at the time of the **Babylonian** captivity. Then, the entire people of **Israel** having been driven into exile, the Temple of God with its entire service was brought to nothing and burned to ashes, and the faithful children of the Lord were given over as a mockery to all the nations and generations of the world, just as the Prophet **Daniel** lamentably presents in his prayer. "That is indeed true," he said. "But if God has now seen fit and decided in His counsel to allow such a thing for a certain time, for the testing of His church and the revealing of those who cling to Him from the heart: do we also think we can prevent such a thing with our untimely anxiety, groundless worries, and ungrateful murmurings? Indeed, we shall much sooner bring even heavier punishment upon our own necks."

Truly, the means to turn God's wrath away from us is not that we run and race anxiously, and carefully trouble our hearts with many things, blaming our misfortune now on one, then on another, and seeking to shake it off our necks by improper means. But on the contrary, that we bow our necks, receive the rod of the Lord <note>The "rod" refers to divine discipline or punishment</note> in humility, and expect our deliverance in hope and stillness.

Nor shall we attribute it again to the clever agility of our enemies, while we know that God Himself moves their hands and directs their weapons for our chastisement; but we shall find all the cause of the misfortune in the deepest depths of our hearts.

And shall he not much sooner and much more be punished, precisely because, knowing it, he did not do it? Luke 12:48. When we read that Pharaoh commanded the children of Israel that they should still complete the number of bricks they had made daily before, even though he provided no straw for them to make them with, Exodus 5, then we judge that to have been a very hard and tyrannical treatment. And even if He spares them for a time for the sake of His name, which they have confessed, He will nonetheless soon—precisely for the sake of the honor of His name—visit, punish, and destroy such a people if they will not repent in time. For He cannot otherwise vindicate the honor of His name, as has now been shown.

It is, therefore, nothing but sheer foolishness that people still vainly imagine that because they have the pure doctrine among them, they shall be spared, even if they bring forth no fruits worthy of that pure doctrine; whereas they ought truly to fear for that very reason, that they shall be punished all the more and all the sooner, and be visited by judgment, if they do not repent at once.

### CHAPTER XII ###

->Answering the fourth<-

<column-break/>

<margin>IV. Objection. Our enemies and opponents are wickedly sinful and worse than we; therefore they shall be attacked first, and thus we have no need to fear them.</margin>
The fourth objection is this: That our enemies are worse than we; they are horrible idolaters <note>In this 17th-century context, "idolaters" usually refers to Roman Catholics, specifically their use of statues and the Mass.</note> and mostly lead a godless life besides. People there kneel before sticks and blocks <note>original: *ſtocken / en blocken*; a derogatory reference to religious icons and statues</note> and images; they are worse than drunkards, and all manner of frivolity increases there so much that it overflows. From this, some on our side conclude that we are in no danger: that even though the Lord stands in a posture of war, has whetted His sword, and bent His bow, He has not aimed it at us so much as at our enemy, who is much worse than we. They argue the enemy also has much innocent blood of the Martyrs on their horns and therefore, by all appearances, shall be the very first to be attacked and severely punished. This sets many people at ease in their conduct, which is not good; and for this very reason, many people delude themselves that no matter how poorly we behave, we are nonetheless in no danger.

<margin>Answer 1. The Lord is often accustomed to chastising His people through a nation that is much worse than they themselves are.</margin>
Answer: We do not doubt that the Lord our God has spared us for a long time and in many ways because of the wickedness of our enemies, and especially so that they should not justify themselves and burden the holy truth (Deuteronomy 32:27-28). But we must not let it rest on that. For the Lord our wise God is also accustomed to punishing His people through those who are worse than they themselves. Listen to how the Prophet Habakkuk, having observed this (namely, that wicked idolaters, who attributed their victory to their idols to the belittling of the God of Israel, Chapter 1:11, had gained the upper hand against the people of God), complains about it in verses 12 and 13: "Are you not from everlasting, O Lord..."

...Lord my God (he says) my Holy One: we shall not die: O Lord, you have appointed him for judgment, and O Rock, you have established him for punishment. You are of purer eyes than to behold evil, and you cannot look upon trouble: why would you look upon those who deal treacherously? why would you remain silent when the wicked swallows up him who is more righteous than himself? & etc. <note>This is a translation of Habakkuk 1:12–13, where the prophet questions why God uses the "wicked" Chaldeans to punish Judah.</note> Mark this: the wicked sometimes swallows up the one who is more pious than he, and that occurs even under the eyes of God Himself, with the Lord God watching over it. Hear also how the Lord God Himself had threatened this in Ezekiel 7:24. Therefore, I will (He says) cause the worst of the Heathens to come, who shall possess their houses as an inheritance, and I will cause the pride of the strong to cease, & etc. So also is the Book of the Lord full of examples of such punishments: read the Book of Judges <note>original: "Judicum"</note>, how many times you find there the people of Israel overpowered by the vile Canaanites and other Heathens, who were nonetheless such completely sunken idol-worshippers that they had neither knowledge nor sign of the true God, which was still to be found within Israel. The same is found in the Books of Kings and the Chronicles.

<margin>2. Likewise, the Lord God has threatened that He will visit His people above all generations, most of all because of their sins.</margin>

And all of this follows the faithful warning which the Lord God has frequently given to His people: namely, that He would indeed visit their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with plagues (Psalm 89:33); that He would indeed punish them most of all, above all other nations, if they did not conduct themselves well. Hear indeed what the Lord says on this subject through the Prophet Amos, against His own people: Out of all

<column-break/>

the generations of the earth, I have known you alone: Therefore I will visit all your iniquities upon you (Amos 3:2). And that is also what the Apostle Paul says: Tribulation and anguish upon every soul of man that works evil, first of the Jew, and also of the Greek (Romans 2:9). And Peter testifies that judgment begins at the house of God (1 Peter 4:17). And Jerusalem, the city of the Great King, the city which is called by His name, she first drinks the bitter cup of hardships before the nations come to drink of it (Jeremiah 25:28, 29).

Thus, we certainly cannot rely on the fact that our enemies are worse than we; for even if they were ten times worse than they are, they are still good enough to punish us; they are indeed good enough to be a rod of the Lord’s anger, and a staff of His fury, to strike us (Isaiah 10:5), and thereby also to fill up the measure of their own sins in us, so that they too, in their own time, shall reach their end and be cast into the fire. For even though the Lord, for His name's sake, may spare His own people for a little while—so that He does not take away their memory from among men, looking upon the wrath of their enemies who might become bold because of it and say, "our power is high, and the Lord God has not done this" (Deuteronomy 32:27, 28)—nevertheless, when His people still continue in their sins, His anger kindles so greatly that even if the enemies should become bold because of it, He will no longer spare His people, just as is evident in all the aforementioned examples.

Specifically, because Jerusalem enjoyed many more means of godliness and received many more blessings from God, she ought to have behaved much better. And because they did not do so, their sin was greatly magnified, to the point that even though their sins, in their own nature, were not as great as those of Samaria and Sodom, they were so weighed down by these circumstances that Sodom and Samaria were made to appear righteous by comparison. *If the signs had been done in Sodom and Gomorrah that were done in the cities of Judah, they would have long ago repented in sackcloth and ashes*, Matthew 11:20, etc. <note>A reference to Jesus’ warning that cities with more spiritual privilege face stricter judgment.</note> So we may rightly maintain that had the ministers of the Word in Rome, in Madrid, and in other prominent cities of the Papists been able to preach the Word of God as freely and abundantly as they have done in Middelburg,

<column-break/>

This greatly aggravates our sin: that while the Trumpet of the Great King <note>A metaphor for the preaching of the Gospel.</note> is among us, and Moses and Aaron <note>Biblical archetypes for religious and civil leadership; here referring to the Dutch ministers and magistrates.</note> lead us, and while we have all means of conversion and improvement in abundance among us, so many still remain unconverted and walk so unseemly. This is evidence of a bad conscience and leads greatly to the blasphemy of the name of the Great God. Thus, our sins are also made heavier by everything we said in the answer to the previous objection. Our own doctrine and confession also imply this: namely, that the wrath of God is kindled against the entire congregation when we—people who have all means at hand to prevent and improve public scandalous sins—nevertheless allow them to take the upper hand among us.

So that they shall be the first in punishment if they are not the first in conversion.

### CHAPTER XIII. ###

#### Answering the fifth objection: namely, that we have seen various signs of God's favor toward us, and that it is therefore not to be feared that God would want to destroy us; for if He had such an intention, He would not have spared us for so long. ####

<margin>
Objection: that the Lord has most graciously delivered us from difficulties during our most unfavorable times.
</margin>
The fifth objection is this: That we have seen various signs of God's special favor toward us in our nation—that He has many times most miraculously delivered us, and held our heads high against our enemies, and that He has even now most graciously delivered us from our most recent difficulties. From this, some conclude, for their own peace of mind, that if the Lord intended to destroy us, He

</margin>
Answer: The Prophet Jeremiah says to sinful Israel: *For the Lord of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced evil against you: because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and of the house of Judah*, Jer. 11:17. So it is nothing new that the Lord God might destroy a people to whom He has previously shown much goodness. Hear further what the Lord says on this subject in Jeremiah 45:4: *Thus says the Lord; Behold, what I have built, I break down, and what I have planted, I pluck up; even this whole land.* Therefore, there is simply no reason why we should flatter ourselves or grow bold in our godlessness and sin, promising ourselves further deliverance just because the Lord helped us so well through the last difficulties. This is certainly a completely distorted conclusion: for if we view it this way, we entirely miss the intention that the Lord our good God had in the deliverance He gave us.

</margin>

<margin>1. Because God's ways in this are unfathomable.</margin>
To that, the general answer is that God’s ways are unfathomable, and that it is nothing but sheer madness, when God's word stands against us, that we would still want to rely on this or that. Who shall say that the congregations of the **Valtellina** <note>original: "Veltoline"; referring to a valley in the Alps where Protestant congregations were violently suppressed and massacred in 1620 during the "Sacro Macello."</note> were not much better than we are? Therefore we must look away from all such things and look straight, like the **Cherubim**, down upon the **Mercy Seat**, beneath which the Tables of the Covenant lie, and see what God says in His Word. If a people should then find that their state was such that God the Lord in His word promises them all good things, then they must not despair, even if they see no great outward appearance of succeeding; but they must hope firmly in the Lord, who will make it right. But if a people should find, from the word of the Lord, that God the Lord stands against them, that he has indeed whetted his sword, his bow—

**Thus** was that excellent Prince in the East-land / the godly **Job** tested / whom the Lord (as the text says) began to ruin in his estate without external cause / to see / if he would then still remain firm in his **piety** <note>original: *vromicheyt*; in the 17th century, this term implied both moral integrity and courageous steadfastness in faith</note>, Job 2:3. her / before she allowed herself to be moved to conversion / and to the abandonment of her wicked ways <note>original: "snoode parten," referring to evil behaviors or "tricks."</note>; He also wants her now to feel / what a pitiful thing it is / to pray, plead, and pursue much and for a long time / yes, to diligently use all means of help / and of healing / and yet not be heard / nor helped; just as she has let the servants of God pray, plead, and pursue her much / and for a long time / and use all means / to convert her / without her wanting to listen or improve herself during all that time. See, this is one reason why the Lord God does not help her immediately / even when she now begins to listen to the Lord / and to observe and consider His means. For it is altogether quite just / that such measure as she has meted out to the Lord her God / and His servants / should also be given to her, **Matthew 7 verses 1, 2.** <note>original: "Matth. 7. vers. 1. 2."</note> and just as she has made the Lord wait a long time / even when He tried all means of improvement upon her / before she would give them place / and accept them; so now the Lord also wants to make her wait / even when she now faithfully considers all the means of healing / before He will immediately bless them / and make them effective. So also the Lord our God delays our healing for great and weighty reasons, and even for our own good and for our salvation, as we may trust. He hides His face from us for a little while longer, so that we might come to ourselves and seek His help and favor all the more zealously and fervently. He delays our healing a bit longer, so that now having turned to Him, we might examine ourselves even more closely and encourage ourselves to use and apply all His means of healing thoroughly. ### CHAPTER I.

->Regarding what is lacking, so that after so many difficulties as have come upon the Church of God these past years, and still press upon it, the same is nevertheless not yet delivered.<-

<margin>It is our bounden duty <note>original: "schuldige plicht," a moral or religious obligation</note> to investigate what is hindering it, that after so many difficulties as have come upon the Church of God these past years and still press upon it: the same is nevertheless not delivered.</margin>
I. How hard it has gone these past years for God's Church, throughout the entire Reformed world, is known to all those who know anything of the affairs of the Christian world: nevertheless, she is the well-beloved of God, in Christ Jesus her Lord; however much the arrogant <note>original: "moedige," here meaning prideful or haughty</note> and ungrateful world may dominate and boast over her. Thus it is also very significant to consider, as we have proven in the previous Treatise, what might be the hindrance that she is not helped; what it might be that keeps the blessing of God from the blessed. Therefore the Prophet Jeremiah speaks in this situation thus: *Who is the wise man, that may understand this? and to whom hath the mouth of the Lord spoken, that he may declare it, for what the land perisheth and is burned up like a wilderness, that none passeth through?*

<column-break/>

<margin>Jer. 9:12</margin>This also serves to be particularly investigated regarding our present situation. See, it is innate to man by nature, when he falls into any trouble and makes every effort to be helped, and yet is not helped, to investigate where the fault may lie. The rough mariners, who were with Jonah on the sea in a tempest, knew to do this, Jonah 1. And when someone among the children of the world has fallen into some strange sickness, and makes great effort to be healed, and finds that it fails, they are immediately ready to believe that some evil is at play; they easily think that they are bewitched <note>original: "betoobert," reflecting the 17th-century belief that persistent illness without a clear cause might be supernatural</note>.

<margin>Proof that it goes very hard now with God's Church.</margin>
II. This applies to us; we are in difficulty; we make great effort to get out of it; we go round by land and sea to obtain means of enlightenment <note>original: "verlichtinge," meaning relief or easing of a burden</note>; and we are not helped; it proceeds from bad to worse. *We looked for peace, but no good came; and for a time of health, and behold, trouble!* Jerem. 14 vs. 19. Nevertheless, *Lord, thou hast been favorable unto thy land, and hast turned away the captivity of Jacob,* Psalm 85:2.

**III.** But now we should find out where we are failing, so that after all these difficulties and after all the means we have employed against them, we are still not helped; thus we must awaken the gift of the Spirit, which is always in the Church of God; namely, the **Spirit of discernment**. <margin>Because sin, which makes us stained, is entirely prevalent, it also blinds us so that we cannot see well what hinders our healing.</margin>

But where sin begins to get the upper hand, there man is wondrously blinded and made unfeeling, as if he had taken a sleeping potion; so that he can only with great difficulty see or feel his faults and defects (being in this condition). He who is mastered by sin walks in darkness and knows not where he goes; he usually judges everything that comes before him incorrectly; he is terrified by this or that which cannot harm him, and that which is most to be feared, he does not see. He will fear a rustling leaf or a running mouse, and yet often does not fear a deadly pitfall that is before his feet. Therefore, it is common with the sickness of the Church that this misfortune is added: that for a time she does not see clearly what harms her most

<column-break/>

and oppresses her. Therefore, we must awaken the **spirit of discernment**, for it truly goes the same way with us.

**IV.** See, there is, beyond the torment of the **Conscience**, a twofold sickness in the Church of God, according to the phrase of Holy Scripture: One is outward—these are the oppressions, dear times <note>original: "diere tijden," referring to periods of inflation, scarcity, or famine</note>, **Pestilence**, and other discomforts—these we see, and we run to remedy them when we are oppressed by them. There is another internal and inward sickness, which is prevailing sin; this we do not see so clearly, nor do we feel it as a sickness, and therefore we are not accustomed to attend to it; which then bears much discomfort—indeed, it entirely hinders her healing.

<margin>The actual reason why we have not been delivered from the difficulties that have struck us so often, and against which we have resisted so much, is this: because until now we have not been improved by these same difficulties.</margin>

**V.** So we say then, that the actual reason why God’s Church, having fallen into great difficulties, still remains in them—no matter how much resistance she offers against them—is this: because through all the difficulties and all the discomforts that have struck her outwardly (of which the world takes most notice and she herself feels most), she has not been improved from her inward sickness, which is the bold sin that has crept upon and seized her, as we have proven in the first Part of this Treatise, Chapter 3.

### FOR ZION'S WOUND

new difficulties break out among us constantly; and from year to year we are exhorted by new hardships—as if by so many reminding Bailiffs <note>original: "Deur-waerders" — officials who serve legal summons or collect debts; here, the author uses them as a metaphor for God's judgments</note> of the Most High God—to pay our vows. If we continue to neglect this, and once we have gained some breathing room from previous hardships, we return with Pharaoh to our old sins (Exod. 8:15), then we are essentially mocking the Lord. We have nothing else to expect but that the Lord will make our bonds tighter and will visit us <note>original: "t' huys soecken" — a term meaning to bring judgment directly to one's own home or community</note> from time to time with even heavier plagues, just as He threatens the mockers (Isa. 28:22).

<margin>
God's Word confirms this to us incontrovertibly.
</margin>
**VIII.** It is also most clearly and plainly testified to us throughout God’s Word that we must truly better ourselves if we wish to be properly helped. It is all too in vain to employ all other means to rescue ourselves from our difficulties if we do not see to it that our sins—which brought us into these difficulties in the first place—are corrected. Hear what the Lord Himself says to this point through the Prophet Jeremiah: "What have you to do," He says, "with the way of Egypt, to drink the waters of Sihor?" <note>original: "Sihors" — referring to the Nile; the prophet is criticizing seeking political alliances with Egypt instead of relying on God</note> as if those were special medicinal waters to cure your sickness; "and what have you to do with the way of Assyria, to drink the waters of the River?" Your own wickedness shall chastise you, and your backslidings shall punish you: know therefore and see that it is an evil and bitter thing that you have forsaken the Lord your God, and that my fear is not in you, says the Lord, the Lord of hosts (Jer. 2:18-19).

<column-break/>

This applies to us. It cannot help us to travel to France and wish to drink of the waters of the Seine; nor can it help us to travel to England and wish to drink of the waters of the Thames <note>The author is criticizing the Dutch Republic's reliance on foreign military and political alliances with France and England rather than seeking spiritual reform</note>. It is the fault of our own wickedness that we are so scourged, and our own disobedience that we are so punished. The evil that oppresses us lies in the very heart of our state; it is our lukewarmness and faint-heartedness in the service of the Most High, our burning zeal in the service of the world, our ambition, lust for status, pride, lasciviousness, wantonness, gluttony, greed, injustice, spite, bitterness, partisanship, unforgiveness, hatred, and envy, and whatever other base whims there may be, with which our Land is flooded as if by a sea. These are the things that do this to us. All in vain do we run far away; the cure must be performed at home, within our own state. There, the firm foundations of our help must be laid.

Read through the entire Book of God, especially the Book of Judges and of Kings; you shall find and realize that it never went well for the people of God when they went running here and there seeking help, as long as they neglected to reform and better that which was disordered at home in their own city. If we are then God's people, we too shall enter that path entirely in vain. Hear once more what the Lord Himself says to this, Hosea 5:13-14: "When Ephraim saw his sickness, and Judah his wound, then Ephraim went to Assyria, and he sent to King Jareb: but he could not [heal you]..."

### BALM OF GILEAD

For where is there a household, a guild, a college <note>The author uses "Collegie" to refer to professional associations or administrative boards.</note>, or an assembly—of whatever nature it might be, in a higher or lower station—which consistently follows the direction of God's Word, and keeps an eye on what the Lord God says in His Word concerning all their actions? Yet we are true Reformed Christians; that is our profession and confession: that all matters must be performed by us according to the Word of the Lord (2 Timothy 3:15, 16, 17). But very few are bound by it, few who bow themselves in continuous obedience under the Word of the Lord to walk according to His counsel. Indeed, everyone acts as master over the precious Word of the Lord; people presume to circumcise and to shorten <note>In this context, the author means "cutting down" or selectively editing the Bible to suit one's own desires.</note> the precious Word of God by which they must live, which the Lord God gives them for the healing of their souls. Truly, the precious Word of God suffers an unbearable arrogance among us these days; many take it up only as far as it pleases their minds and is convenient to practice; the rest they reject and leave aside. Indeed, do we not see this daily, that wicked, ungrateful people presume throughout to bend and adapt the Holy Ordinances, Laws, and Rules of God’s precious Word under the wicked customs, ways of acting, habits, and practices of the damnable world? Is there a meal to be held, or a wedding? What order does one follow? That which God prescribes in His Word, or that which is in vogue through the custom of the corrupt world? Experience teaches us: God's rule and order are pushed to one

side and excluded; and the wicked practice of the world is followed. And thus it goes in a thousand cases everywhere; thus is God’s Word despised, mistreated, and spat upon. Our conscience knows that it happens so. But what do we think? Will the Lord God tolerate that? Will He let that pass unavenged? Shall the great God, out of great grace and mercy, give us His holy, precious Word for our preservation and salvation (if we would conduct our affairs according to the counsel of the Lord revealed to us in His Word), and shall we despise it? Shall we dare to exalt the damnable practices of the world above the wholesome ordinances of God’s Word, and will that go well for us? The Lord God puts us to the test through His Word, to see in what estimation and esteem we hold Him; if He sees that we despise His Word, He takes it as if we despised Him Himself. Then He will neither bless nor deliver us, but rather punish us even more until we improve. ### VI. Great Political Ambition /

<margin>6. Great ambition.</margin>
<note>The original Dutch term *staetsuchticheydt* literally means "state-sickness," referring to an obsessive craving for high office or political status.</note>
everyone who can barely even crawl along / immediately fancies himself / to be a man fit to rule a country; everyone considers himself worthy of the best position. Whereas in former times / the Lord God fetched the Regents of his people / from the sheepfold / from among the lambs / *Exodus 3:1-2 and Psalm 78:70, 72.* from the prison / *Genesis 41:14.* and from the threshing floor / *Judges 6:11-12.* before they themselves sought it; now they are found in great numbers of that sort / who come seeking it themselves. David would not do this / *Psalm 131.* This is also a high-reaching sin / directly contrary to the required **Humility** / and **Lowliness** of true Christians; through which everyone ought to think lowly of himself / and associate with the humble, *Romans 12:16.* doing nothing through strife, or vain glory; but through humility considering one another better than himself, *Philippians 2:3.* and outdoing one another in all honor.

And this wretched ambition penetrates so deeply / like a gnawing cancer / that it affects not only each individual / but also all friends who, with ambition / seek to promote and exalt their own. Thus it happens daily / that while everyone seeks to promote himself / or his own blood / or his favored friend / or acquaintance; many positions are occupied / and possessed by such / who are far too narrow / and too thin in gifts / and capacity / to fulfill their places and ministries; to the unspeakable damage / and detriment of the common good. <note>The "common good" (*het gemeyne beste*) was a central concept in Dutch political thought, referring to the collective welfare and stability of the Republic.</note> For while everyone is only out / to maintain his own house / thus are there in the

<column-break/>

Civil Government and Church / posts and pillars joined / that do not stand firm / that are not healthy at the heart within / and have no strength / to bear the weight that is laid upon them / therefore the entire house is in peril / that it may soon come falling upon our heads. All the more / because through this partisan favoritism / it happens time and again / that among God's people / in all kinds of ministries and positions / ministers are forced upon God / who do not please him / in whom he takes no delight; since so little heed is paid to his counsel (which he gave to his people through Jethro / long ago) *Exodus 18:21.* <note>Jethro, the father-in-law of Moses, advised him to select capable, God-fearing men who "hate dishonest gain" to serve as officials.</note> therefore he also turns his blessing away from such ministry / and business / which then necessarily burdens the land most severely. For it is indeed the Lord alone who must help us; if we then make him an adversary of our business / then our affairs cannot go well. It would be something / if we could, along with the position given to a man / also give the gift / to fulfill that position / just as God the Lord can do. But now, when friends and kinsmen / through their meddling / have promoted this or that person to a position / they must, alas / leave the man as he is / and the Land and the Church must use him / as they find him: God has not called him to it / and those who promoted him to it / cannot give him the gifts; so in the end it all results in great damage / and detriment to the common good. So that in this case the common cause may well say / as Jacob once said in another situation / *all things are against me, Genesis 42:36.*

### VII. Great excess in clothing, meals, and all kinds of pride, practiced wantonness, and profligacy.

<margin>7. Great excess in clothing and meals.</margin>
For notwithstanding these heavy times, and that the Lord God calls us on all sides to fasting, prayer, and mourning; yet we break out in all lightheartedness, as if in defiance of God. He cuts away <note>original: *besnijt*, literally "prunes" or "circumcises"</note> our abundance, yet we will not give up our excess; this provokes the Lord our God—who is far too powerful for us—exceedingly much. *Isaiah 22:12-13 and Amos 6:4-6.* And this is even more the case because these sins are so boldly committed, even though the people are so faithfully warned against them in many places; and where they might also hear, in many places, of so many hungry and naked members of Christ <note>A common metaphor referring to fellow believers as parts of the "Body of Christ."</note> whom they ought to feed and clothe, by cutting back on their own superfluities, which they could spare as easily as the clippings of their fingernails. Therefore it shall also be very difficult to answer for the fact that many members of Christ have lived and sat in great misery and distress for a long time, due to the lack of those means which these people

<column-break/>

have so uselessly squandered. So this is also a high-reaching sin, and provokes God the Lord exceedingly much, to come and snatch from the hands of these people the means which they so greatly misuse, and to hand over the same, along with their persons, to be plundered by their enemies. Your men shall fall by the sword, and your mighty men in the battle. And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she, being desolate, shall sit upon the ground. *Isaiah 3:24-26.*

### VIII. Great self-seeking; 
since everyone seeks to gain their own advantage over their neighbor to the utmost. Because of this, the land is filled with dishonest trade, deceit, lying words, false goods, <term>weights</term><note>The use of inaccurate scales or "false weights" to cheat customers, a practice frequently condemned in biblical law.</note>, and everything that is worthless; all of which are <term>crying sins</term><note>original: *krijschende sonden*. To this end, many people persist in following paths I know not what, which are not good. From this also come the <term>evasion of excises</term><note>Tax fraud regarding internal taxes on consumer goods like beer, wine, or cloth.</note>, taxes, etc., heavy failures, bankruptcies, and a thousand troubles. Thus, this self-seeking—which the Apostle so faithfully warns all Christians against in *Philippians 2:4*—is alone powerful enough to ruin an entire country over time. Provision must be made for this, and those who can be significantly caught in this (and all diligence must be applied to that end) should be

<column-break/>

punished in such a way that others might take them as a proper example, and learn to fear doing such evil among the people of God.

### IX. And see, these are the evil and deadly <term>humors</term><note>In early modern medicine, "humors" were bodily fluids like blood or bile. An imbalance was thought to cause disease; here, the author uses it as a metaphor for spiritual and moral corruption in the body politic.</note>
with which the people of God in our time are so burdened that they shall not and cannot be healed or recover until these same wicked, evil humors are cleansed and purged from them. Therefore, special attention must be paid to this; for these have gained such an upper hand among us that they are hardly recognized as sins; or at least those who are most guilty of them (as everyone can see) nonetheless want to know nothing of it. People can hardly bear it when one speaks against these sins. We have fallen into such a rut that we would rather endure the sickness than the remedies for the sickness; which is then a certain omen of approaching ruin, if one is not on one's guard in time and does not seek to improve. For we have surely heard enough by now that the Lord our God will not stop; indeed, He will visit us more and more if we do not cease from our sins in good time and apply ourselves to reforming and bettering these base, evil sins, *Leviticus 26:18-19.*

### X. Therefore, we wish from our whole heart
that we might yet become wise in time and understand such things, and that we—like children of a good <term>disposition</term><note>original: *in-borst*, referring to a person's innate character or natural inclination.</note>—would improve ourselves through fewer strikes and punishments, and yield to the hand of the Lord; so that we might prevent and escape greater and heavier plagues. That would truly be most easy for our peace.

For truly, in this the Lord wants to do as a wise **physician** <note>original: *Medetijn-meester*</note> is accustomed to deal with his Patient: when the purgation <note>A medical treatment intended to "cleanse" the body of harmful humors, often through laxatives or emetics.</note> he has given does not work, or does not work enough, and he notices that the body is still full of bad humors, then he prescribes new Recipes again, and even stronger ones. Therefore, we must yet pay good attention everywhere to those two other duties that still lie before us to practice when the **Daughter of Zion** <note>A biblical personification of the people of Israel or the Church.</note> is sick, when the people of God are in misfortune and contempt, and to take those also to heart. Namely, that we heartily mourn over the misfortune of the people of God, and faithfully lend a hand to improve it.

**VII.** And it is in every respect very noteworthy how great the earnestness of the Lord our Heavenly Father is, that the sickness of the Daughter of Zion <note>The "Daughter of Zion" is a poetic biblical personification of the people of Israel or the Christian Church.</note> might be healed—that His people might indeed be delivered from their distress and difficulties. The Lord (as we have heard in the first part of this Treatise) provides for this both the Balm and the Physician <note>original: "Heel-meester" — literally 'healing-master,' a common term for a surgeon or physician</note>; He spares no expense (so to speak), and He shuns no effort. To this end He sends His word, the most precious thing the world can receive; He sends His Prophets, who are most dear to Him; so busily (spoken with all reverence) does our great God occupy Himself with healing His sick people.

<column-break/>

And He demonstrates this most of all by the fact that He has sent His own Son to heal them with His heart’s blood.

<margin>
The Holy God has arranged the restoration and healing of Zion’s Daughter so wonderfully so that we should take notice and better take it to heart.
</margin>

**1.** Yea, the Lord our great and only wise God has so managed the whole work of healing His people that it is full of wonders and remarkable things, so that we should certainly not let it pass by unobserved and, through lack of notice, perish. What can be found more wonderful than the Person of our supreme Physician Himself—even the Lord Jesus, who is God and man in one Person? Where does one ever hear of a physician <note>original: "Medecijn-meester"</note> who is accustomed to pour out his own heart’s blood to heal his patients? If we then further observe the conduct of our God in this matter, it is surely most wonderful. The all-sufficient God Himself stands by His people with counsel, and commands, and beseeches, and prays that they would please take this, His healing Medicine, made from the heart’s blood of His own Son; and when that does not happen immediately, the Lord complains about it, threatens, promises, wishes it were so, and calls heaven and earth to witness such stupidity, Isaiah 1:2, 3. Anyone can sufficiently grasp what a wonderful conduct this is of our great God. The means through which the Lord our God offers this Medicine to His people, which is His holy word, is also full of wonders, Psalm 119:18. His Prophets, who deliver this word, He also makes—through strange and rare conduct—into "signs and wonders" <note>original: "wonder-teeckenen"</note> among His people, Psalm 71:7, Ezekiel 24.

Why else, than to cause curious people <note>The author suggests God uses "wondrous" or strange providences to pique the interest of the worldly, drawing them toward spiritual healing.</note> to pay attention to it through these means, and by paying attention, to be won over, so that they might be healed. See how very great the earnestness is with God, that His people might indeed be helped when they are in need and in difficulty. How then do we not also realize that it is also our bounden duty to be followers of God as beloved children? (Ephesians 5:1). That we also contribute whatever we can and may to help God’s people when they are in need; that we indeed sharpen our utmost ingenuity and understanding to that end, turning and bending ourselves into all forms and fashions that can exist with a good conscience, in order to do good to the people of God.

<margin>
Indeed, the entire Book of God is essentially concerned above all with the affairs of God's people and God’s dealings toward them.
</margin>

2. Indeed, what is more, if one pays proper attention to it, one perceives everywhere in the Book of God (in the Book of God, I say, which is the wisdom of God and is alone worthy of being well-considered) there one perceives everywhere that the Lord God Almighty, who made the ends of the earth, passes by all other things as if unregarded, and keeps Himself busy and concerned only with His Church and people. Read from the beginning of Genesis to the end of Revelation, and you shall find that the Book of God throughout mentions and speaks of the condition of the people of God. In <term>Genesis</term><note>The author provides a "biography" of the Church using the books of the Bible.</note> the birth and the first nurturing of the Daughter of Zion is recounted; in <term>Exodus</term> the removal of this Daughter into a better climate, out of the land of Egypt, where her breasts grew,

<column-break/>

Ezekiel 23:3, and yet she was treated too harshly. In <term>Leviticus</term>, <term>Numbers</term>, and <term>Deuteronomy</term>, her struggles in the wilderness are told, where the Lord tested her love (Jeremiah 2:2) and prescribed laws and rules for her to follow, so that she might always prosper. Furthermore, what is the book of <term>Joshua</term> other than the account of the establishment of this Daughter in her possession of the promised land, against all opposing power, with heaven and earth helping her therein? # BALSEM GILEADS

...and then in the Holy Scripture, very great and **striking** things—according to the world's judgment—are recounted very simply and as if only in passing; whereas, on the other hand, often very small things concerning God's people are pointed out very exactly, such as how Jacob kept house with his wives and children, and so on. Do we not see here again how very much the Lord God occupies Himself with His Church?

Are we not then also reasonably convinced by this that we likewise must apply our greatest thoughts, writings, and meditations to the service of God's people?

<margin>And all the work of God, in the governance of the world, is arranged according to the condition of God’s people.</margin>

3. And just as the Lord God thus arranges and appoints His whole Word solely according to the condition of His Church; so He also does with His whole work. For whoever observes God's actual operations in this with a discerning eye will immediately find that the **Governance** of the whole world is so managed and appointed by God that it all tends toward and serves the well-being of His people and Church. For their sake, the Lord God will stir the whole world. When He wanted His people to rise up in Egypt, He stirred up a famine in all the surrounding lands; when He wanted to lead them out again, He stirred and troubled the whole land of Egypt; when He wanted to give them the land of Canaan, He cleared out all the peoples and nations that were in it; when He wanted to discipline them again, He stirred up powerful Tyrants here and there; and when He wanted to lead them to Babylon, He first went to devastate many Kingdoms and Territories that lay in between to prepare the way for it.

<column-break/>

So also the Lord God allows the world to remain standing now for no other reason than that He might still fulfill what He has promised to His people, and so that from time to time He might still cause those He has chosen for His people to enter in, 2 Peter 3 verses 8 and 9. From this, it is once again evident that the Lord our great God occupies Himself most diligently with the **Daughter of Zion**, with His people.

Just as we also see here in our text, the great God conducts Himself regarding the condition of the sick Daughter of Zion as if He had nothing else to care for but the sick Daughter of Zion. Indeed, He conducts Himself everywhere in such a way that it is fully evident in every respect that the Lord our great God (be it spoken with reverence) is wonderfully moved and touched by it. The inner mercies <note>original: "innicheden" - a term referring to deep, internal compassion or the "yearnings" of the soul.</note> of our God, so to speak, are stirred over it; *Is there no Balm in Gilead? Is there no Physician there? For why is the health of the daughter of my people not recovered?* Would the Lord our great God, who best knows the value of things, apply such great earnestness and diligence to the condition of the sick Daughter of Zion if it were not worth the effort? Consider then further: shall the Lord our great God be thus powerfully moved, and thus take to heart the miserable state of His people, and apply such great earnestness to make them come out of their difficulties—shall indeed the <term>bowels [inghewant]: a 17th-century term for the seat of deep emotion and compassion</term> of this God be stirred, and His heart wonderfully break out over His people when they fall into misfortune—and shall we not take it to heart!

->BALM OF GILEAD<-

As concerns the internal and spiritual distress of the **Church of God**, which consists of the willful, **crying sins** <note>Sins so grave they are said to "cry out" to heaven for justice.</note> that have crept in among so many of the people of God during their time of luxury and prosperity; against these we must apply all those Divine means that we pointed out and treated at length in the first part of this treatise. The principal means of healing is the **healing and most precious blood of the Son of God**; the ministerial means are true repentance, faith, and prayer; the subordinate means are **God’s Word**, strengthened by holy Baptism and the Lord’s Supper; the example of the pious, the discipline of the Church, the punishment of the authorities, and God’s own chastisements, when rightly received. Behold, all these means the Lord God points out to us in His word, through which the people of God might be healed and helped from their sins; each being useful in its own place and order for the removal of the sin that makes the people of God sick. Thus, all these means must be well applied by all those who are heartily desirous of doing some good for the people of God and helping to rescue them from their distress and difficulties; we shall therefore proceed to point out what remains to be done.

III. No one can believe more than what has been promised to him by God in His word; therefore the word of God is called the "word of faith," Romans 10:8. Now, in the word of the Lord, no promise has been made to anyone that they shall be healed through the precious blood of the Son of God, except only to those who turn away from the sins in Jacob <note>A biblical reference to the community of the faithful; "Jacob" is a poetic name for the people of God.</note>, as has been shown above; so also no one can assure themselves through faith that they shall be healed from the sickness of their soul, unless it be that they are minded to turn away from the sins in Jacob; therefore the Prophet Hosea admonished the people of God: first, that they should turn to their God, keep mercy and justice, and that they should then continually wait for their God, Hosea 12:6. This is not to say that man can properly repent without faith, but that man, for his comfort and healing, cannot sensibly claim or assure himself on any ground of God’s word that God wants to help and heal him, unless he feels this wrought within him: that he is sincerely resolved to turn himself from his evil ways to his God, and is minded to cast away (as much as is in him, as much as is possible) all his transgressions wherewith he has transgressed.

## CHAPTER IX.
### Concerning faith in God, which we must practice for the sake of healing.

<margin>We must also strive to assure ourselves through faith that, by turning back to God, the Lord our God will help us out of all our difficulties.</margin>
I. **T**hirdly, since the practice of conversion is directed toward putting us in such a state that we might—based on the reliable testimony of God’s word—believe that God the Lord wants to help and heal us through the precious blood of His Son; so, in every respect, special effort must be made so that the sick Daughter of Zion <note>A poetic biblical title for the Church or the community of believers.</note>, now turning her heart to God, might also assure herself in her heart that the Lord our gracious God truly wishes to heal and restore her. For He has indeed clearly testified that whenever we return to Him, He will heal our backslidings, *Jeremiah 3:22*, and that He will indeed heal our waywardness and love us freely, *Hosea 14:2 and 5.*

Oh! This also deserves proper attention; many of those who truly love the Daughter of Zion, seeing the wound she has received through sinful entanglements, and observing the cunning malice of many of her enemies who are intent on destroying her to the core, lose heart. They think that all is lost and that the end of these troubles will be the total ruin of the Church. But truly, there is no need to think this way. If there were no God in heaven, we might rightfully think so; but as long as the Lord our God reigns, who is so well able to help and heal, the sick Daughter of Zion need not lose hope for her recovery. Let her only practice

<column-break/>

this: namely, that she turn her heart from her evil ways to God, and further commit her way unto the Lord; He shall bring it to pass, *Psalm 37:5.* For when the Church of God thus relies upon the Lord her God, then God's word, God's truth, and God's honor are pledged <note>original: "ge-engagert"</note> to help her. For the Lord our God cannot deny Himself, and He has promised that He will help such as these, *Psalm 37:3, 4, 5; Psalm 91:14, etc.*

<margin>For regardless of how far our affairs have been lost, the Lord can easily help us, if He only wills it.</margin>
II. What if our affairs were in such a great decline that it seemed entirely impossible in our own eyes that we should ever be helped or healed? Would it therefore also be impossible for the Lord our God? *Zechariah 8:6.* What if our enemies are many and powerful, rising up against us? What if they have "strong horns" <note>A biblical metaphor for power or prideful strength.</note> to push us and wound us more and more? The Lord can quickly cause "four smiths" to appear against them, to cast down all those horns, *Zechariah 1:21.* What if they seem as strong as iron and bronze? The Lord can somewhere cause iron to appear that shall break the iron of the north and the bronze, *Jeremiah 15:12.* Indeed, what if the wound our enemies have given us seems entirely deadly and incurable? Does not the Lord God still have with Him the sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ, which can even cleanse from dead works, *Hebrews 9:14*, and bring the dead to life? Even if things had declined so far with us that we were not only as if dead, but even as if entirely [wasted] by death...

So also many a person complains about the disorder that is in his wife, children, or in other members of the household, yet he neglects to practice the household prayers with steady persistence among his housemates. ### CHAPTER XII.
### Of the Holy Sacraments, which must also be used correctly, so that God's people might be helped.

Improve this then, all you who desire to be healed: use both Holy Baptism and the Holy Supper, and use them to be made better, and that shall do your soul good; then it shall happen to you according to your faith.

All those who love and wish well for God’s people must be of the mind that all those who lead an un-Christian life while making a Christian profession are certainly the most harmful instruments that can emerge to distress God’s Church. They are indeed surely like **foxes**, even **little foxes**, that destroy the **Vineyards** <note>original: "vossen... kleyne vossen... Wijngaerde" - a reference to Song of Solomon 2:15, a common metaphor for heretics or moral transgressors</note>. They are like plague-stricken persons, fit to bring a whole Congregation under the Plague of God; they are like **scabby sheep**, capable of corrupting a whole flock. Therefore, Discipline must be applied against such people, so that their unhealthiness does not eat further in like a **cancer** <note>The author uses "cancker" here in the archaic sense of a spreading, gangrenous sore.</note>.

<margin>
For truly, the slackness regarding these people has caused much trouble for God’s people in our age.
</margin>

II. We cannot doubt that through the failure to properly apply this means, the **Reformed Church** <term>Gereformeerde Kercke: The established Protestant church in the Dutch Republic</term> has also been brought into great misfortune and contempt. I do not know how our hearts

It is testified that there are people by the dozens in large Congregations (besides the Absentees who are mere brawlers, gluttons, and drunkards) who are constant visitors of taverns and gambling houses. We hear such things, yet we do not know exactly where the trouble is rooted or where they are to be found. But here and there we meet one who, upon being admonished, will readily say: "There are twenty more who act just as badly as I do, and whom you leave unbothered." I believe they do not always speak the truth; nevertheless, there is some truth to it. But now, if we properly remembered the example of **Achan** <note>A biblical figure who stole forbidden items, causing God's anger to fall upon the whole army of Israel (Joshua 7).</note>, who by sinning in Israel stirred up a wrath over the whole assembly; "and he did not die alone in his iniquity," (Joshua 22:20). If we indeed observed one another according to the demand of Christian Discipline, in order to raise up the fallen again, would it then go this way with us? Well may we then ask here, as the Apostle once did (1 Corinthians 6:5) in a similar situation: "Is there then none among us who is wise, not even one," who could track down such **scabby sheep** and provide a remedy against them? Is there not one zealous man who steps into the breach against these destructive **foxes** (Ezekiel 13:4-5), so that the fence of the Lord be not entirely broken down and His Congregation laid waste? Oh, oh, that everyone would take courage here! For how shall we proceed to the prevention and clearing out of such **outcasts** <note>original: "Catharmata" (Greek: καθάρματα) - literally "scum" or "refuse," often referring to people sacrificed or cast out to purify a city.</note>, of such shameful spots—
